segments.heading: Myth 1
segments.narration: Myth: you have to itemize. Fact: self-employed health insurance is an adjustment to income, on Form seventy-two oh six, with the standard deduction too.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a form with a heart. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Myth 2
segments.narration: Myth: it lowers self-employment tax. Fact: it lowers income tax only.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. two coins, one crossed out. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Limits
segments.narration: It can't exceed your business profit, and months you could join an employer's plan, yours or a spouse's, don't count.

script.cta: Follow for one freelancer money move a week.
script.caption:
Hunt week 7: self-employed health insurance premiums are an adjustment to income (Form 7206), so you don't need to itemize. They lower income tax, not self-employment tax, can't exceed business profit, and don't count for months you were eligible for an employer-subsidized plan (yours or a spouse's). Example (fictional): single, $60,000 of profit, no other income, 2026 federal figures, from the site's tax model. $5,000 of premiums lowers federal tax by about $480.

Educational, not tax advice. 2026 federal figures; check your state.
